This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com
Up to 2,000 characters. 2,000 remaining.

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Interactive Counter

This counter demonstrates state management and ARIA live regions for accessible dynamic content.

content.text:
I made six targeted fixes to `0.html`, but none of them are tested: the syntax check I tried to run on the inline scripts was blocked by the session's permissions, and I haven't opened the page in a browser.

## What changed

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Removed the stray `:root[data-theme] { color-scheme: light dark; }` block | It outranked the print stylesheet's `color-scheme: light`, so a saved theme plus a dark OS could print with dark form controls. |
| Submit button now uses `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled` while sending | `disabled` drops keyboard focus from the button in some browsers. A guard at the top of the submit handler still blocks double submission. |
| Removed the `#form-status[aria-label*="Error"]` rule | Nothing ever sets that attribute, so the rule was dead. |
| Replaced `.button:disabled` with `button[aria-disabled="true"]` | Links can't be disabled, so the old selector never matched. |
| Removed the duplicate `button:focus-visible` rule | The global `:focus-visible` rule already does the same thing. |
| Printed link URLs now render inline with no margin | They were inheriting the inline-block layout of the ↗ icon, so long URLs wrapped badly. |
| Removed the `og:image` meta tag | Social crawlers need an `http(s)` URL; the `data:` URI was ignored. |

I also changed the button text from `Sending...` to `Sending…`.

## Left for you

- **Canonical URL:** `https://www.example.com` is still a placeholder. Set it to the real URL, and add `og:url` and a hosted `og:image` when you have them.
- **Author meta:** `<meta name="author">` publishes your email address, while the JSON-LD uses "K. Smith". Use the name in both if the page is going public.
- **Theme variables:** the dark palette is defined twice. `light-dark()` would remove the duplication, but it breaks colours in Safari before 17.5, so I left it alone.
